.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 231 AM EDT Monday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 231 AM EDT Monday...

1. Rounds of showers will continue throughout the day today, 
with conditions trending drier for Tuesday and mid-week as high 
pressure builds into the region

2. Our next chance for rain will be with a cold frontal passage 
Thursday into Friday, followed by cooler weather for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 231 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Another day of cool and showery weather is expected 
across the region today as additional rounds of showers move through 
the region as the system to our south slowly drifts eastward. 
Greatest rainfall amounts for today are expected across eastern and 
southern Vermont, where totals are expected to be between 0.25 and 
0.5 inches of rain, while northern New York looks to remain on the 
drier side. The showers and cloud cover will keep temperatures on 
the cool side for this time of year, with highs only climbing into 
the upper 50s and low 60s. 

Shower activity will gradually wane through the evening and 
overnight hours tonight as the low shifts away, with drier weather 
conditions expected to prevail throughout much of the day Tuesday as 
high pressure begins to build into the region. The drier conditions 
are expected to continue through much of the week, with temperatures 
gradually trending warmer as well. High temperatures on Tuesday will 
only be in the 50s and lower 60s again, but by Thursday widespread 
highs in the 70s are expected.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A cold front will make its way southward across our 
region late Thursday into Friday, bringing increasing chances of 
precipitation along with it. The best forcing will remain well to 
our north, so anticipate scattered to perhaps widespread showers, 
mostly light to occasionally moderate in nature. Thunder is not 
anticipated given the unfavorable timing of the frontal passage 
(overnight Thu into early Fri AM). High pressure will immediately 
follow the front, ushering in a drier and cooler airmass for at 
least the first half of the weekend. Sunday is a bit less certain; 
the 00z GFS and to a lesser extent, the 00z CMC indicate a wave of 
precipitation lifting into our region sometime Sunday. The 
deterministic GFS is the most aggressive with this feature, though 
it does the support of a few of its ensemble members, along with 
some GEPS members, as well. Didn't get a chance to look at the 00z 
ECMWF, but the 12z run held off any precipitation until Sunday 
night/Monday, though again, some of its ensemble members show a 
rainy and cool Sunday. Given these differences, have stayed with the 
WPC/NBM forecast, which gives low chance PoPs for Sunday. 
Temperatures will be warmest on Friday, in the mid 60s to near 70F, 
then trending cooler with highs in the 60s and lows in the low 30s 
to low 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 12Z Tuesday...Scattered showers will persist through the
first several hours of the TAF period, becoming more widespread
through day, particularly after 18z. A mix of VFR/MVFR ceilings
early in the period will eventually lower to MVFR at all 
terminals as moisture increases. Can't rule out IFR conditions, 
especially after 00z Tue. Have gone with ceilings below 1000 ft
at MPV/SLK/RUT where confidence in IFR is highest. Showers have
mainly been handled with PROB30 given the scattered nature, but
prevailing -SHRA has been included for portions of the 
afternoon at most terminals. Visibility mainly 4-6SM in any 
precipitation. Rain will wind down after 23z, but wouldn't be 
surprised for lingering fog or drizzle overnight. N/NE winds 
remain light through the period, mainly less than 10 kt. 

Outlook...

Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&
